 Health News Thousands in Georgia expected to drop ACA plans as open enrollment begins
 This is the second year of major premium increases. Enrollment in Georgia Access is down one-third since Jan. 1. Open enrollment began Sunday. Share Monthly premiums will spike by up to 29% for Georgians who purchase their health insurance plans from the state’s Affordable Care Act marketplace, according to state data obtained by The Atlanta Journal-Constitution. (Georgia Access website) By Tamar Hallerman 3 hours ago Organizations that help people sign up for health insurance on Georgia’s Affordable Care Act marketplace are expecting many of their clients to balk at the substantial price increases unveiled during the open enrollment period, which began Sunday. 
 The eight insurers participating in Georgia Access, the state’s Obamacare marketplace, recently finalized 2027 rates that are 11% to 29% higher than last year. Rates will vary based on age, location and other factors, but the average statewide premium will be nearly $932 per month, up roughly 51% from two years ago.
